name: Ameil Sheridan
title: Product Designer
summary: Product designer with 4+ years designing enterprise SaaS, AI and healthcare products. I research the messy middle of complex workflows, turn it into clear flows and reusable systems, and work closely with engineers to ship it.

lookingFor.setup: Open to remote, hybrid and international teams
lookingFor.strengths: Enterprise workflows, AI-assisted UX, design systems, healthcare and regulated products

experience.where: Kuala Lumpur, working with teams across Asia Pacific and Europe
experience.about: Global Expansion Platform (GEP), an enterprise product that helps companies manage legal entities across many countries.
highlights: Designing AI-assisted workflows for GEP, including Smart Fill, AI suggestion cards with confidence scores and provenance badges that separate AI-filled from manually entered values.
Redesigned Service Tracker and the Appoint Director service request: a three-step flow, jurisdiction-aware fields for BVI, Singapore and Hong Kong, and milestone tracking for multi-entity requests.
Building GeniOS, the design library for GEP's AI workflows, combining existing GEP components with new AI-native patterns such as the Geni assistant panel.
Maintaining components and guidelines: tables, modals, toasts, navigation, upload and download, and accessibility fixes.

experience.about: PhIS 3.0, the pharmacy information system redesign built for the NPRA.
highlights: Led design for the PhIS 3.0 redesign, from research and flows to high-fidelity screens.
Designed visit management, patient admission and role-based homepages for clerks and nurses.

experience.about: Map-based monitoring systems and dashboards for infrastructure and government clients.
highlights: Designed map-based dashboards and internal tools, turning spatial and project data into everyday interfaces.
Ran GIS analysis alongside interface design, so the data and the UI were shaped together.

education.title: Bachelor of Arts (Geography)
education.note: Spatial analysis and GIS: where my habit of mapping whole systems before the details began.
